title: Drug Gang Attacks Force Hundreds of Indigenous Families to Flee Communities
detail: Drug cartel attacks have forced hundreds of Indigenous families to abandon their communities across Mexico, according to Guardian reporting from Mexico City on May 11, 2026. Armed criminal groups — operating in areas where Indigenous communities have resisted cartel extortion, land seizures, and forced recruitment — mounted assaults that displaced entire villages. The violence reflects a broader pattern of cartels targeting Indigenous communities in Guerrero, Oaxaca, Chiapas, and other states where traditional governance structures and self-defense 'autodefensa' groups have attempted to push back against organized crime. Displaced families face acute humanitarian needs with limited access to shelter, food, and legal protection. Human rights organizations have called on the federal government to provide emergency assistance and security guarantees for return. The displacement adds to Mexico's growing internal displacement crisis, with the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) tracking over 400,000 Mexicans displaced by violence since 2019.

media.caption: Drug gang attacks force hundreds of Indigenous families to flee their communities in Mexico
